before:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & -9 & -3 & 6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -6 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & -9 & -3 & 6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -9 & -3 & 6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -3 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x,$ and we have two free variables, $y$ and $z.$ That means we can find $x$ in terms of $y$ and $z.$ 

Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*. 

As a result, only statement III is true.

$$

before:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $A$, that is, the rows of ${A}^{T}.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of ${A}^{T},$ it must be orthogonal to each row of ${A}^{T}.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by ${A}^{T},$ we actually multiply each row of ${A}^{T}$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}(A)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $A,$ which is $\text{Null}({A}^{T}).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."
